objective: Evaluate pinned local ZaloPay Vietnamese F5-TTS on CUDA with the owner-authorized Hina MP3 reference, promote it only if real speech quality passes, and otherwise keep VieNeu CUDA as the safe default.
non_goals: Do not claim that zero-shot reference conditioning is model-weight fine-tuning.
Do not expose arbitrary voice upload or clone endpoints.
Do not retain generated speech or chat text.
Do not claim ElevenLabs-equivalent quality before owner listening and a later blind benchmark.
contracts: F5-TTS uses only the fixed hash-bound Hina synthetic reference and explicit transcript.
The production desktop path is CUDA-only and fails loudly instead of falling back to CPU.
Complete text still passes pre_tts moderation before provider inference.
A failed F5 real-audio quality gate must keep VieNeu CUDA as the desktop default.
Runtime audio remains in memory; the explicit smoke tool alone may write a WAV under var/tmp.
allowed_dependencies: Existing PyTorch CUDA, ffmpeg and soundfile runtime
acceptance_criteria: Speech unit tests cover pinned F5 snapshots, reference hash validation and 24 kHz PCM output.
Real CUDA smoke and round-trip STT determine whether the ZaloPay checkpoint produces intelligible Vietnamese instead of merely a structurally valid WAV.
Desktop labels identify the provider actually selected by the launcher.
Model, dependency and voice provenance identify exact revisions, licenses and local-only candidate status.
